title: CyberEvolver: Structured Self-Evolution for Cybersecurity Agents On the Fly

mechanism.domainTask: On-policy self-evolution of LLM cybersecurity agents for CTF, penetration testing, and vulnerability exploitation
mechanism.populationDetail: A per-target beam maintains multiple agent variants; parent IDs are recorded in a global evolution tree, but beam membership is flat per generation.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The top-K variants by within-generation progress score are selected as parents; no separate archive outside the beam is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Invalid children are discarded; valid children generated from selected parents form the next beam generation.
mechanism.generationDetail: One selected parent scaffold is revised through sequential strategy, interface, domain-knowledge, and perception-layer mutation calls; each child can change multiple layers.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Executable success verification is supplemented by a diagnosis-derived 0-100 relative progress score used to compare variants and condition mutations.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Top-K agents are selected by relative progress score; each selected parent independently produces multiple children.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Layer-attributed diagnosis of long execution trajectories produces counterfactual mutation signals for on-policy cybersecurity scaffold evolution.

provenance.sourcePdf: additional_papers/202605/CyberEvolver Structured Self-Evolution for Cybersecurity Agents On the Fly.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Four backbones are benchmarked separately, not combined in one search run. The progress score is a relative signal within a generation, not an absolute distance-to-success objective.
